title: Students protest RSS leader's presence at Central University of Kerala

tea.why: Students opposed the presence of an RSS-linked leader at a university seminar and claimed registered students were denied entry.
tea.want: Protesters demanded that the programme be called off and opposed the event.
tea.changed: Oct 8: Bekal police registered a case against 25 unidentified students following the seminar protests.

summary: Students at the Central University of Kerala in Kasaragod staged demonstrations against the presence of an RSS-linked figure at a seminar about the Vande Mataram national song. Activists from student groups including KSU, MSF, SFI, and AISF participated, contending that registered students were wrongfully barred from attending. Protesters shouted slogans, clashed with police at the venue, and disrupted proceedings. According to police, a case was registered against approximately 25 unidentified students for unlawful assembly and rioting. Tensions also involved a verbal confrontation between ABVP members and opposition student activists. University officials and political leaders offered differing accounts of the campus events.
response: Police used physical removal and registered a case against 25 unidentified students under sections related to unlawful assembly, rioting, and disobedience. Police stated they denied any injuries occurred during the protests.

arrests.text: A case has been registered against 25 students who are yet to be identified.

updates.text: Students held demonstrations against an RSS-linked leader's presence at a university seminar and clashed with police.
Police registered a case against 25 unidentified students following campus disruptions during the Vande Mataram seminar.
